back: A named memory location holding a value that can change while the program runs.
A named value set when declared that cannot change while the program runs, e.g. CONSTANT Discount ← 0.1.
The kind of data held (INTEGER, REAL, CHAR, STRING, BOOLEAN); it decides storage and allowed operations.
INTEGER: whole numbers (25, -3). REAL: numbers with a fractional part, always written with a digit each side of the point (12.0, 0.5).
CHAR: exactly one character in single quotes ('Y'). STRING: zero or more characters in double quotes ("Harare", "").
They are never used in arithmetic and may start with 0 or contain spaces, so store them as STRING.

DECLARE Total : INTEGER
CONSTANT Rate ← 0.15 (literal values only)
Total ← Total + Price: the right side is worked out first and stored in the variable on the left. = is only for comparing.
Use a third variable: Temp ← A, A ← B, B ← Temp. Without Temp both end up with the same value.
Syntax: the grammar rules of a language. Semantics: the meaning, what a correct statement actually does.
